raw.assessment: The incumbent provides embedded-caption previews and retained history, and succeeds within 15 minutes in 20/30 sessions, below the required 27/30. Its strongest supplied limiting observation is H1-O7: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in five to 11 minutes without version uncertainty. Thus full rendering can support usable previews in a bounded workflow; universal replacement is not established. Completion inversions and unexpected source versions suggest coordination or identification problems, but do not establish their cause. The 49-hour week does not establish festival capacity.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: capture an immutable video-and-caption revision tuple at request time, render exactly those retained sources, and display that same tuple on the completed preview and download entry. This could prevent source drift and make intended previews identifiable despite completion order.
openings.delta: Adds explicit source identity across request, execution and selection while retaining the incumbent render and history workflow.
openings.prediction: With interleaved video and caption edits and deliberately reversed completion order, each artifact matches its recorded tuple and editors select their intended tuple.
openings.probe: Use fabricated footage in private staging; submit overlapping revisions, verify output source hashes and caption wording, and have the two editors identify previews. Check continued access to the last delivered wording. Measure implementation effort and processing overhead before adoption.
assumptions: Existing storage can retain immutable source revisions.
The change fits four engineer-days, one editor-day and the 80-hour allowance; unverified.

openings.claim: Do slow sessions primarily lose time before the intended artifact becomes available, or after availability while identifying and reviewing it?
openings.delta: Distinguishes render scheduling remedies from preview identification remedies.
openings.prediction: A waiting-dominant explanation predicts availability near or beyond 15 minutes; an identification-dominant explanation predicts earlier availability followed by prolonged selection or review.
openings.probe: Align timestamped render events with intended source tuples and timed editor demonstrations; partition final-edit-to-correct-preview time at artifact availability, recording selection and viewing separately.
assumptions: A short private-staging demonstration fits the available editor-day.
Demonstrations can discriminate mechanisms but cannot establish the 30-session success measure.

raw.assessment: The stipulated observations support investigating render ordering and version identification together, but do not establish how much delay comes from either. One combined mechanism merits testing; feasibility within the allotted engineering time remains unverified.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: cross immutable video-and-caption manifests with a replaceable pending-render slot at the queue-to-preview-history interface. Each save binds exact retained input versions into a manifest; the pending slot points to the newest intended manifest. Workers render that manifest, and completion can acquire the current-preview label only if its manifest still matches the editor's intended pair. Other completions remain explicitly identified in history. Pin the last delivered manifest, preview, and original caption text separately.
openings.delta: Manifests alone identify versions but leave redundant work queued; coalescing alone shortens the queue but cannot establish which input pair a completion contains. Using the manifest as both scheduling identity and publication condition couples reduced pending work to correct preview identification even when completion order reverses.
openings.prediction: Against either mechanism alone, the combination should reduce time to an unmistakably identified intended preview under burst edits and reversed completions. It should not relabel an obsolete completion as current. The size of the benefit, including whether 27 of 30 sessions meet 15 minutes, is unknown.
openings.probe: Within the four engineer-days and one editor-day, use private staging, demonstration footage, and timestamped events to compare baseline, manifests only, coalescing only, and their combination. Include caption bursts, video-cut switches, and deliberately reversed completions. Compare render count, time to the intended pair, editor identification errors, and retained delivered wording. Verify rendered inputs against each manifest. If implementation fits the budget, measure the stated acceptance criteria over 30 new editing sessions; stop processing at the weekly allowance rather than assuming festival capacity.
assumptions: Existing storage and workers can retain immutable inputs and conditionally publish a completion within four engineer-days.
Enough saves arrive before pending work starts for coalescing to help; running renders need not be cancelled.
All content remains on existing private accounts, and the existing embedded-caption delivery renderer remains available.
Editors can understand the paired-version label within the available evaluation time.

openings.claim: Bind retained video/caption revisions immutably through request, rendering and displayed identity. Optionally coalesce pending requests to the intended manifest; only matching completions become current. Identify other completions in history; pin delivered preview, manifest and original wording.
openings.discriminator: Manifests prevent source drift and identify pairs; coalescing reduces redundant pending work; publication matching prevents obsolete completions becoming current. Compare these separately and together.
openings.fit: Private accounts, embedded-caption renderer and delivered-version access preserved; four engineer-days, one editor-day and processing fit unverified.
openings.probe: Compare baseline, manifests only, coalescing only and combination in private staging with fabricated footage, burst edits, cut switches and reversed completions. Check hashes, wording, editor identification, render counts, elapsed time, retained delivery and effort.
openings.uncertainty: Immutable retention and conditional publication feasibility, label comprehension and savings unknown. Coalescing helps only pending work; running renders need not cancel.

openings.claim: Determine whether delay occurs before intended-artifact availability or during selection and viewing.
openings.discriminator: Late availability favors scheduling remedies; early availability followed by delay favors identification/review remedies.
openings.fit: Private demonstrations assumed to fit editor-day.
openings.probe: Align render timestamps with intended tuples; time availability, selection and viewing separately.
openings.uncertainty: Demonstrations discriminate causes but cannot establish 30-session acceptance.

lineage.reason: Identity mechanism retained as standalone comparator.
Pending coalescing, conditional publication and delivered-version pin retained.

post_distill.decision: Probe causes and feasibility first; single-correction success limits replacement claims. If feasible, verify 27/30 within 15 minutes and zero unintended pairs; stop at 80 processing hours/week. Festival demand remains unknown.
